plan: 1 Samuel 30:1-31; 1 Chronicles 12:20-22; 1 Samuel 31:1-13; 1 Chronicles 10:1-14; 1 Chronicles 9:40-44; 2 Samuel 4:4; 2 Samuel 1:1-16, 17-27

readings.title: The Raid on Tsiqlag
readings.subtitle: Dawid Pursues the Amalĕqites
readings.text: [1 Samuel 30:1] And it came to be, when Dawid and his men came to Tsiqlag, on the third day, that the Amalĕqites had invaded the South and Tsiqlag, and smitten <dn>את</dn> Tsiqlag and burned it with fire, [2] and had taken captive <dn>את</dn> the women and <dn>את</dn> those who were there, from small to great. They did not kill anyone, but led them away and went their way. [3] And Dawid and his men came to the city and saw it burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive. [4] And Dawid and the people who were with him lifted up <dn>את</dn> their voices and wept, until they had no more power to weep. [5] And Dawid’s two wives, Aḥino‛am the Yizre‛ĕlitess, and Aḇigayil the widow of Naḇal the Karmelite, had been taken captive. [6] And Dawid was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, each for his sons and his daughters. But Dawid strengthened himself in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn>. [7] And Dawid said to Eḇyathar the priest, son of Aḥimeleḵ, “Please bring <dn>את</dn> the ephod here to me.” And Eḇyathar brought <dn>את</dn> the ephod to Dawid. [8] And Dawid inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Do I pursue <dn>את</dn> this troop? Do I overtake them?” And <dn>He</dn> answered him, <dq>“Pursue, for you shall certainly overtake them and certainly rescue.”</dq> [9] So Dawid went, he and the six hundred men who were <dn>את</dn> with him, and came to the wadi Besor, where those left behind stood still. [10] And Dawid pursued, he and four hundred men, for two hundred stayed behind, who were too exhausted to cross <dn>את</dn> the wadi Besor. [11] And they found an Mitsrite in the field, and brought him to Dawid, and gave him bread and he ate, and they let him drink water, [12] and gave him a piece of a cake of figs and two clusters of raisins. And he ate and his spirit returned to him, for he had not eaten bread nor drunk water for three days and three nights. [13] And Dawid said to him, “To whom do you belong, and where are you from?” And he said, “I am a young man from Mitsrayim, servant of an Amalĕqite, and my master left me behind, because I became sick three days ago. [14] “We invaded the southern area of the Kerĕthites, and the territory which belongs to Yehudah, and the southern area of Kalĕḇ, and we burned <dn>את</dn> Tsiqlag with fire.” [15] And Dawid said to him, “Could you bring me down to this troop?” And he said, “Swear to me by <dn>Elohim</dn> that you neither kill me nor deliver me into the hands of my master, then I bring you down to this troop.”

readings.title: The Recovery
readings.subtitle: Dawid Distributes the Spoil
readings.text: [1 Samuel 30:16] And he brought him down and saw them spread out over all the land, eating and drinking and dancing, because of all the great spoil which they had taken from the land of the Pelishtites and from the land of Yehudah. [17] And Dawid smote them from twilight until the evening of the next day. And none of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode on camels and fled. [18] And Dawid rescued <dn>את</dn> all that the Amalĕqites had taken. Dawid also rescued <dn>את</dn> his two wives. [19] And there was nothing lacking to them, from small to great, to sons and daughters, to spoil and <dn>את</dn> whatever they had taken from them – Dawid recovered <dn>את</dn> all. [20] And Dawid took <dn>את</dn> all the flocks and herds they had driven before those other livestock, and they said, “This is Dawid’s spoil.” [21] And Dawid came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow Dawid, who also had been left behind at the wadi Besor. And they went out to meet Dawid and to meet <dn>את</dn> the people who were with him. And Dawid came near the people and greeted them. [22] Then all the evil and worthless men of those who went with Dawid answered and said, “Because they did not go with us, we do not give them any of the spoil that we have recovered, except for every man’s <dn>את</dn> wife and <dn>את</dn> children, that they might lead them away and go.” [23] But Dawid said, “My brothers, you do not do so with <dn>את</dn> what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given us, who has guarded us and delivered into our hand <dn>את</dn> the troop that came against us. [24] “And who would listen to you in this matter? For as his portion is who goes down to the battle, so is his portion who stays by the baggage, they share alike.” [25] And so it was, from that day forward, he made it a law and a right-ruling for Yisra’ĕl to this day. [26] And Dawid came to Tsiqlag, and he sent some of the spoil to the elders of Yehudah, to his friends, saying, “Here is a present for you from the spoil of the enemies of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>” – [27] to those in Bĕyth Ěl, and to those in Ramoth of the South, and to those in Yattir, [28] and to those in Aro‛ĕr, and to those in Siphmoth, and to those in Eshtemoa, [29] and to those in Raḵal, and to those in the cities of the Yeraḥme’ĕlites, and to those in the cities of the Qĕynites, [30] and to those in Ḥormah, and to those in Bor Ashan, and to those in Athaḵ, [31] and to those in Ḥeḇron, and to all the places where Dawid himself and his men walked about.

readings.title: Mighty Men Join Dawid
readings.subtitle: The Camp of Elohim
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 12:20] As he went to Tsiqlag, there defected to him from Menashsheh: Aḏnah, and Yozaḇaḏ, and Yeḏi‛a’ĕl, and Miḵa’ĕl, and Yozaḇaḏ, and Elihu, and Tsilthai, heads of the thousands who were of Menashsheh. [21] And they helped Dawid against the raiding bands, for they were all mighty brave men, and they were commanders in the army. [22] For day by day they came to Dawid to help him, until it was a great camp, like the camp of <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Fall of Sha’ul
readings.subtitle: Defeat on Mount Gilboa
readings.text: [1 Samuel 31:1] And the Pelishtites fought against Yisra’ĕl. And the men of Yisra’ĕl fled from before the Pelishtites, and fell slain on Mount Gilboa. [2] And the Pelishtites followed hard after <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul and after <dn>את</dn> his sons. And the Pelishtites smote <dn>את</dn> Yehonathan, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇinaḏaḇ, and <dn>את</dn> Malkishua, sons of Sha’ul. [3] And the battle was heavy against Sha’ul, and the archers hit him, and he was severely wounded by the archers. [4] And Sha’ul said to his armour-bearer, “Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and thrust me through and abuse me.” But his armour-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Sha’ul took <dn>את</dn> a sword and fell on it. [5] And when his armour-bearer saw that Sha’ul was dead, he also fell on his sword, and died with him. [6] Thus Sha’ul and his three sons and his armour-bearer, and all his men died together that day. [7] And when the men of Yisra’ĕl who were beyond the valley, and those who were beyond the Yardĕn, saw that the men of Yisra’ĕl had fled and that Sha’ul and his sons were dead, they forsook <dn>את</dn> the cities and fled. And the Pelishtites came and dwelt in them. [8] And it came to be the next day, that the Pelishtites came to strip <dn>את</dn> the slain, and they found <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul and <dn>את</dn> his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa. [9] And they cut off <dn>את</dn> his head and stripped off <dn>את</dn> his armour, and sent word throughout the land of the Pelishtites, to declare it in the house of their idols and to the people. [10] And they put <dn>את</dn> his armour in the house of Ashtaroth, and they fastened <dn>את</dn> his body to the wall of Bĕyth Shan. [11] And when the inhabitants of Yaḇĕsh Gil‛aḏ heard what the Pelishtites had done to Sha’ul, [12] all the brave men arose and went all night, and took <dn>את</dn> the body of Sha’ul and <dn>את</dn> the bodies of his sons from the wall of Bĕyth Shan. And they came to Yaḇĕsh and burned them there. [13] And they took <dn>את</dn> their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Yaḇĕsh, and fasted seven days.

readings.title: The Chronicle of Sha'ul's Death
readings.subtitle: The Cost of Transgression
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 10:1] And the Pelishtites fought against Yisra’ĕl. And the men of Yisra’ĕl fled from before the Pelishtites, and fell slain on Mount Gilboa. [2] And the Pelishtites followed hard after Sha’ul and after his sons. And the Pelishtites smote <dn>את</dn> Yehonathan, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇinaḏaḇ, and <dn>את</dn> Malkishua, sons of Sha’ul. [3] And the battle was heavy against Sha’ul, and the archers hit him, and he was wounded by the archers. [4] And Sha’ul said to his armour-bearer, “Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and abuse me.” But his armour-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Sha’ul took <dn>את</dn> the sword and fell on it. [5] And when his armour-bearer saw that Sha’ul was dead, he also fell on his sword and died. [6] Thus Sha’ul died with his three sons, and all his house died together. [7] And when all the men of Yisra’ĕl who were in the valley saw that they had fled and that Sha’ul and his sons were dead, they forsook their cities and fled. And the Pelishtites came and dwelt in them. [8] And it came to be the next day, that the Pelishtites came to strip <dn>את</dn> the slain, and they found <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul and <dn>את</dn> his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa. [9] And they stripped him and took <dn>את</dn> his head and <dn>את</dn> his armour, and sent word throughout the land of the Pelishtites to declare the news to their idols and to the people. [10] And they put <dn>את</dn> his armour in the house of their mighty ones, and fastened <dn>את</dn> his head in the house of Dagon. [11] And when all Yaḇĕsh Gil‛aḏ heard <dn>את</dn> all that the Pelishtites had done to Sha’ul, [12] all the brave men arose and took <dn>את</dn> the body of Sha’ul and <dn>את</dn> the bodies of his sons. And they brought them to Yaḇĕsh, and buried <dn>את</dn> their bones under the tamarisk tree at Yaḇĕsh, and fasted seven days. [13] And Sha’ul died for his trespass which he had trespassed against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because of the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which he did not guard, and also for asking a medium for inquiry, [14] and did not inquire of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Therefore <dn>He</dn> put him to death, and turned <dn>את</dn> the reign over to Dawid son of Yishai.

readings.title: The Surviving Line of Yehonathan
readings.subtitle: Mephiḇosheth is Spared
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 9:40] And the son of Yehonathan was Meriḇ-Ba‛al, and Meriḇ-Ba‛al brought forth <dn>את</dn> Miḵah. [41] And the sons of Miḵah: Pithon, and Meleḵ, and Taḥrea, and Aḥaz. [42] And Aḥaz brought forth <dn>את</dn> Ya‛rah, and Ya‛rah brought forth <dn>את</dn> Alemeth, and <dn>את</dn> Azmaweth, and <dn>את</dn> Zimri. And Zimri brought forth <dn>את</dn> Motsa, [43] and Motsa brought forth <dn>את</dn> Bin‛a, and Rephayah his son, El‛asah his son, Atsĕl his son. [44] And Atsĕl had six sons whose names were these: Azriqam, Boḵeru, and Yishma‛ĕl, and She‛aryah, and Oḇadyah, and Ḥanan. These were the sons of Atsĕl. [2 Samuel 4:4] And Yehonathan, son of Sha’ul, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news about Sha’ul and Yehonathan came from Yizre‛ĕl. And his nurse took him up and fled. And it came to be, as she made haste to flee, that he fell and became lame. And his name was Mephiḇosheth.

readings.title: The Messenger at Tsiqlag
readings.subtitle: News of the Defeat on Gilboa
readings.text: [2 Samuel 1:1] And it came to be after the death of Sha’ul, when Dawid had returned from the smiting of <dn>את</dn> the Amalĕqites, and Dawid had stayed two days in Tsiqlag, [2] that on the third day, see, a man came from Sha’ul’s camp with his garments torn and dust on his head. And it came to be, when he came to Dawid, that he fell to the ground and did obeisance. [3] And Dawid said to him, “Where do you come from?” So he said to him, “I have escaped from the camp of Yisra’ĕl.” [4] And Dawid said to him, “How did the matter go? Please tell me.” And he answered, “The people have fled from the battle, and many of the people have fallen and died, and Sha’ul and Yehonathan his son are dead too.” [5] And Dawid said to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Sha’ul and Yehonathan his son are dead?” [6] And the young man who told him said, “As I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, there was Sha’ul, leaning on his spear, and see, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him. [7] “And when he looked behind him, he saw me and called to me, and I answered, ‘Here I am.’ [8] “And he said to me, ‘Who are you?’ So I answered him, ‘I am an Amalĕqite.’ [9] “He said to me again, ‘Please stand over me and kill me, for weakness has come upon me, but my life is still in me.’ [10] “So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew that he would not live after he had fallen. And I took <dn>את</dn> the crown that was on his head and <dn>את</dn> the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them here to my master.” [11] Dawid then took hold of his own garments and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him. [12] And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Sha’ul and for Yehonathan his son, and for the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and for the house of Yisra’ĕl, because they had fallen by the sword. [13] And Dawid said to the young man who told him, “Where are you from?” And he answered, “I am the son of a stranger, an Amalĕqite.” [14] And Dawid said to him, “How is it you were not afraid to put forth your hand to destroy <dn>את</dn> the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [15] And Dawid called one of the young men and said, “Go near, and fall on him!” And he smote him so that he died. [16] And Dawid said to him, “Your blood is on your own head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I have killed <dn>את</dn> the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”

readings.title: The Song of the Bow
readings.subtitle: Dawid's Lament for Sha'ul and Yehonathan
readings.text: [2 Samuel 1:17] And Dawid lamented <dn>את</dn> with this lamentation over Sha’ul and over Yehonathan his son, [18] and he said to teach the children of Yehudah the Song of the Bow. See, it is written in the Book of Yashar: [19] “The splendour of Yisra’ĕl is slain on your high places! How the mighty have fallen! [20] “Declare it not in Gath, proclaim it not in the streets of Ashqelon, lest the daughters of the Pelishtites rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult. [21] “O mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew nor rain upon you, nor fields of offerings. For the shield of the mighty was defiled there, the shield of Sha’ul, not anointed with oil. [22] “From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Yehonathan did not turn back, and the sword of Sha’ul did not return empty. [23] “Sha’ul and Yehonathan, beloved and pleasant in their life, and in their death they were not parted. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions. [24] “O daughters of Yisra’ĕl, weep over Sha’ul, who clothed you in scarlet, with refinements, who put ornaments of gold on your garments. [25] “How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle! Yehonathan was slain in your high places. [26] “I am distressed for you, my brother Yehonathan. You were very pleasant to me. Your love to me was wonderful, surpassing the love of women. [27] “How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of battle perished!”
